story.summaryEn: Williams team principal James Vowles has admitted the team "got carried away" with its success last season, but insists the disappointing 2026 campaign is merely "a blip".
detailZh: 詹姆斯·沃尔斯：威廉姆斯领队承认车队因成功而得意忘形，但表示2026赛季F1的挣扎只是“小挫折”
观看或收听《The Fast and the Curious》最新一期节目，听威廉姆斯领队詹姆斯·沃尔斯谈论车队2026年的困境、他为何有信心已经走出低谷，以及他希望F1成本上限规则做出的调整
在《The Fast and the Curious》播客中，威廉姆斯车队领队詹姆斯·沃尔斯与Christian Hewgil对谈，回应了关于其职位压力的评论。
威廉姆斯车队领队詹姆斯·沃尔斯承认车队上赛季因成功而“得意忘形”，但他坚称2026赛季的低迷只是“小挫折”。
沃尔斯在2023年初从梅赛德斯加盟后接管了威廉姆斯车队，并在车队于2025年制造商积分榜上获得第五名时似乎产生了巨大的积极影响，这是他们自2017年以来的最佳成绩。
然而，这项运动历史上最大的规则变革——同时引入了新的动力单元和底盘——导致威廉姆斯车队退步，让车手卡洛斯·塞恩斯和亚历克斯·阿尔本感到非常沮丧。

在2026赛季还剩三轮的情况下，他们在11支车队中排名第九，仅获得12分，与一年前最终137分的总分相比相形见绌。
亚历克斯·阿尔本在五号弯撞墙，导致阿塞拜疆大奖赛出动安全车。
沃尔斯在最新一期《速度与好奇》播客节目中表示：“前进道路上难免会有小波折。不幸的是，我认为这就是一次小波折。”
我认为经历这些是件好事，因为我们已经在车队后方做出了相当大的改变，在我看来，我们必须经历这些才能迈出下一步。
我认为去年我们有些得意忘形了，这恰恰说明当情况没有太大变化时，我们有能力造出一辆还算不错的赛车。但规则变化总会让你暴露无遗。
威廉姆斯车队领队詹姆斯·沃尔斯在《Fast and the Curious》播客中与克里斯蒂安·休吉尔交谈时表示，成本上限正在拉大车队之间的差距，并导致F1不再是一项“健康的运动”。
尽管威廉姆斯的挣扎引发了外界对沃尔斯职位稳定性的猜测，但这位47岁的领队坚称自己并未感到压力。
沃尔斯说：“当我签约加入时，我与董事会达成了一项协议，那就是当我们开始全力推进时，我们会发现一些糟糕的事情。这不是一个我们可以走出去、完全预测我们在不同阶段会处于什么位置的行业。”
“但我会奉献我的心灵、灵魂和每一天的每一小时，团队也会如此，一旦发现问题就全力解决。但我请求作为回报，在这方面能得到背后的支持。”
威廉姆斯的卡洛斯·塞恩斯在阿塞拜疆大奖赛练习赛中刹车起火后被迫进入维修区。
“我必须说，董事会一直非常出色，真的，以至于我记得在冬天，一个相当糟糕的冬天，我每周工作七天，每天工作16、18个小时，那很艰难。我打电话给他们所有人。而一切只是‘我们在这里支持你。我们能帮什么忙？’仅此而已。”
“这不是一个人们会掉以轻心的环境。他们知道这将是一项艰巨的挑战。我早就知道这会是一项艰巨的挑战。我向全世界保证，我们所做的一切在方向上都是正确的，都是为了我们的未来。”

detailEn: James Vowles: Williams boss admits team got carried away with success but says 2026 F1 season struggles are only 'a blip'

Watch or listen to the latest episode of The Fast and the Curious to hear Williams boss James Vowles discuss the team's 2026 struggles, why he is confident a corner has been turned, and the changes he wants to see made to F1's cost cap rules
Joining Christian Hewgil on the Fast and the Curious podcast, Williams Team Principal James Vowles responds to comments on the pressure of his position.
Williams team principal James Vowles has admitted his squad "got carried away" with their success last season but insists a disappointing 2026 campaign is merely "a blip".

Vowles took charge of Williams after joining from Mercedes at the start of 2023 and appeared to be having a hugely positive impact when the team finished fifth in the 2025 constructors' standings, which was their best finish since 2017.

However, the biggest regulation change in the sport's history, which saw the introduction of both new power units and chassis, has seen Williams regress, leaving drivers Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon hugely frustrated.

They are ninth of the 11 teams with three rounds of the 2026 season remaining and have scored just 12 points, which compares poorly to a final total of 137 a year earlier.
Alex Albon found himself in the wall at Turn Five, bringing out the safety car at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
Appearing on the latest episode of The Fast and the Curious podcast, Vowles said: "There's going to be blips in the pathway. This is what I consider a blip, unfortunately.
"And I think it's a good thing we went through it because we've made some pretty enormous changes in the backside of the team, which we had to go through, in my opinion, to make the next steps.

"And I think we got carried away a little bit with ourselves last year, demonstrating that actually when things aren't changing too much, we have the ability to produce a half decent car. But regulation changes will always expose you."

Joining Christian Hewgil on the Fast and the Curious podcast, Williams Team Principal James Vowles says that the cost cap is making the gap between teams bigger and is leading to F1 not being a 'healthy sport'.
Despite Williams' struggles leading to speculation over the security of Vowles' job, the 47-year-old insists that he is not feeling the pressure.

"When I signed up to this, I had an agreement with the board that we're going to find some horrible things when we start pushing ourselves," Vowles said. "It's not a business where we can go out there and completely predict where we're going to be in different phases.
"But I will dedicate my heart, soul and every hour of my day, as will the team into fixing it when we find it. But I ask in return that there's a support behind us in that way.
Williams' Carlos Sainz was forced to enter pits after a fire on his brakes during practice at Azerbaijan GP.

"And I have to say that the board has been outstanding, really, to the extent where I remember in winter, a pretty horrible time in winter, I was working seven day weeks and 16-hour, 18-hour days, it was hard. I called to see all of them. And all it was, was just really a 'we're here behind you. How can we help?' That was it.

"It is not an environment where people are taking this light-heartedly. They know that this is going to be a difficult challenge. I knew it was going to be a difficult challenge. My assurance to the world is everything we are doing is directionally correct for our future."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

detailEn: Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest in final practice from George Russell as Mercedes domination continues ahead of qualifying

Kimi Antonelli led George Russell in another Mercedes one-two in final practice at the Lusail International Circuit; watch Qualifying at 6pm later on Saturday and the Qatar Grand Prix at 4pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports F1

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
